newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - TECHS TARGET 1.8175/85 IN TOPPY DLR/MARK.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - TECHS TARGET 1.8175/85 IN TOPPY DLR/MARK.

text.p: Breaks of several key support levels on Wednesday leave an ailing dollar/mark vulnerable to further losses in the days ahead, with technicians targetting the 1.8175/85 area near-term.
That represents a 50 percent retracement of the move from July 10 lows of 1.7456 to dollar/mark's recent multi-year high of 1.8913, reached on August 6.
A drop below 1.8175/85 would open the door for a test of the next strong support area which comes in at the 1.80 mark level.

"You have a topping pattern which probably directs dollar/mark lower through next week but I'm betting we'll find some value between 1.80 and 1.8180," said Ben Morden, technical analyst at I.D.E.A. Inc.
Morden said the recent bout of volatility was characteristic of a topping pattern, but remained optimistic that dollar/mark would resume its uptrend after additional consolidation.

Dollar/mark crumbled through 1.8430 neckline support of a three-week old head-and-shoulders pattern on Wednesday, setting off stops which ultimately pushed the rate through a two-week up-trend line support level of 1.8385 which dated back to July 29.
Scott Siller, a senior technical analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch, said that 1.8420/50 should limit dollar/mark's upside in the near-term.
"We're a bit oversold on the hourly indicators," he said. "So 1.8175 would be our minimum target and the measured move of the pattern is 1.80 and from there we'd look for fresh strength."
At 1500 EDT/1900 GMT the dollar was changing hands at 1.8345/55 marks, down from 1.8440/50 at the open and 1.8625/35 at Tuesday's close.
